Second, no anthro term may be added to positional_fit as a bonus at observed positions: OAA already contains arm and legs, and the earlier arm gate NO-SHIPPED raw arm-by-position on throw-context confounding (1.94 mph adjusted spread against a 3.80 within-position SD) that this study does not remove. models.surface: /arbitration/ Projections + Arbitration History
models.predicts: the one-year salary an arbitration-eligible player receives for a season in which he is TENDERED a contract and the figure is settled or awarded through the arbitration process, conditional on tender, in deflated dollars
models.champion: two-stage: arb-1 is a ridge level model on log deflated salary with a Duan smearing correction; arb-2-and-later is an empirical raise multiplier banded on (step, prior-salary band), because the per-player model was a measured NULL there. The CBA maximum-cut rule is imposed as a transformed target, z = log(ratio - 0.795), not a clamp, so every prediction and every band endpoint is legal by construction
models.baseline: arb-1: an intercept plus one WAR term (a lag baseline is the wrong bar for a first trip and paired only 199 of 513 rows). arb-2+: the median deflated step multiplier off the prior salary, floored at the maximum cut and the league minimum
models.metric: MdAPE on deflated dollars, forward-chained by arbitration class year over 4 folds, against a per-statistic-class MDE95 floor measured by a paired bootstrap that resamples train AND test clustered on PLAYER and refits every draw
models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-08-09. arb-1 PASSES at 3.29x its floor (MdAPE 0.2545 vs 0.4284) and clears its zero-information control by 2.08x, where the control permutes the production block within (season, arb-step) cells and keeps prior salary, step and season attached. That control still gains +0.084 on its own, so roughly 39% of the naive model-beats-baseline margin is STRUCTURE rather than player production. || arb-2-and-later is a NULL at 0.83x its floor and the board therefore serves the banded multiplier there, not the model. Permuting production makes the arb2+ model WORSE than the baseline, so signal exists; the margin is simply below the floor. Power limit, recorded as a null. || A6 NULL, and the most useful number here: on 261 settled seasons where MLB Trade Rumors published a Matt Swartz projection, Swartz reads MdAPE 0.0811 against our 0.2156 - 2.66x more accurate, consistently at every step (arb1 0.0851/0.2183, arb2 0.0822/0.2038, arb3 0.0758/0.2112). Not mysterious: Swartz prices the counting stats arbitration panels reward and this champion excludes them because nothing here projects them forward, which is what lets one model serve both a backtest and a forecast. Swartz is the better estimate of a KNOWN season and does not exist for an unplayed one. || SCOPE: only seasons whose arbitration step comes from published service time are scored (2022-2026, 1,043 rows, 585 players). Substitute sources measure 0.66 and 0.70 agreement against that ground truth and agree with each other 53%, so the planned 2011-2026 backtest is WITHDRAWN. || Projections past 2026 assume the 2022 CBA structure survives its 2026-12-01 expiry; that is not estimated from data and no published interval covers it.

models.notes: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, registered 2026-07-29. This row carries no eval artifact ON PURPOSE: no measurement supports a predictive reading of the panel, and the one that exists refutes it. Three caveats must stay visible wherever it renders. (1) The strata are the output of a search over 3,957 overlapping cuts with no multiplicity correction, so extreme-looking groups are expected under the null. (2) The source artifact tools/_comb_out/archetype_descriptive_hit.json carries a health_warning claiming every stratum has a statistically zero out-of-fold residual against the shipped eFV model. That claim is FALSE as written: 477 of the 3,957 rows carry |t| >= 2 and 124 carry |t| >= 3. Do not repeat it in copy. (3) The script that produced that artifact, tools/_comb_sweep_desc.py, is ABSENT from the tree and nothing else in the repo writes that file, so mean WAR, median WAR, bust rate and the residual t cannot be regenerated or independently audited; they are a frozen quote of a 2026-07-25 measurement. Stratum MEMBERSHIP is reproducible and archetype_comps_export.py re-checks it on every run against the pre-registered outcome-blind enumeration (all 3,957 ids and resolved-row counts match, prereg sha16 fa70f4244573730b). Hitters only, decision years 2016-2024, 904 rows with 527 at a complete six-year window, reporting floor 25 complete-window players, base mean 1.90 WAR and 76.7 percent bust rate. Reader-facing methodology: glossary entry archetype_comps. SHIPPED FORM (archetype_comps_export.py): the false health_warning is dropped rather than propagated, and each stratum instead carries a reliability tier derived from its own t: priced 3,193 (|t| under 1.645, comps and grade agree), watch 687 (nominally off-model but not surviving Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05 across all 3,957 tests, so unverified rather than a finding), off_model 77 (survives BH at |t| >= 3.30, comps and grade disagree, neither authoritative). Expected counts under a true global null are about 180 at |t| >= 2 and 11 at |t| >= 3, so the excess is real and is NOT purely a multiplicity artifact. Read the off_model tier with its shape attached: 76 of 77 carry a NEGATIVE residual and 43 busted at 100 percent, because WAR floors near zero for a player who never debuts, so any positive expectation on a young low-grade group is guaranteed a one-sided residual. That is the outcome scale bottoming out, not a correctable eFV defect, and the nested-CV NO SHIP verdict stands over all of it. 130 strata carry a zero-width WAR interval (every closed member realized the same value); degenerate, not precise.

Channel C1 (total_fv_instances counted with NO date filter at consensus.py:1248-1252 and passed as one scalar to every event date at :1298) moves 117 rows, mean abs 3.10 FV, max 10.42; the mechanism was hand-derived on tyler_skaggs (full-history instances 2 suppresses the FV-35 pull, as-of 1 fires it, 66.25 -> 58.333). Channel C3 (grade-norm thin-cell pooling) moves 2,286 rows, mean +0.940. CHANNEL C2 IS FALSE, AND THE REASON IS A BIGGER DEFECT THAN THE ONE IT DISPROVES: the drop-off detector matches a legacy '_org_' slug that occurs 0 times in 54,061 snapshots, so dropped_off_pairs returns the empty set on every run and the (fv+30)/2 shrink HAS NEVER FIRED IN PRODUCTION. C3's repair is BLOCKED pending an owner decision: FanGraphs FV, the normalization reference, does not exist in the DB before 2017-02-15, so the as-of remapper returns None there and turns normalization OFF rather than computing an honest as-of offset, which would inject a 3 to 4 FV pre/post-2017 discontinuity into the model's dominant feature. OPEN ITEM: this row's own eval_artifact measures the weighting choice rather than blend-vs-single-source, so the pointer and the baseline do not describe the same experiment; realigning them is an owner call, not a documentation edit. INPUT DEFECT FOUND 2026-07-30 (Phase 5.3 ingestion audit, docs/efv-2026-07-30/POSITION_ROLE_GATE.md, NOT FIXED - registered for an owner call): source `baseballamerica_statcast_by_age` writes a FABRICATED flat FV 40.0 (source_articles.py:230, our own editorial-standout floor, not a Baseball America grade) and votes in avg_fv at full weight 1.0 like a published grade. THIRD CONSEQUENCE: 7 players (braylon_whitaker, easton_shelton, jacob_friend, jake_cunningham, jose_meza, mason_guerra, michael_martinez) have exactly ONE snapshot in the entire database - this one - and were on the board only because we graded them ourselves; with no FV and no rank they have no consensus point and LEAVE the board (ranks 373-1383, none in the top 300). Nothing is served differently until the next ingest re-parses the drop file and the UPSERT writes fv=NULL. performance_ingest was audited in the same pass and CLEARED: flat FV 35 on 2,798 rows but only 30 collisions, i.e. it functions as the ungraded floor it was designed to be.

IDENTITY: a systemic bind-time hole, FOUND 2026-08-04 and NOT yet closed. stats._apply_collision_guard has three checks and BOTH of the ones that matter require a DURABLE binding to already exist: check 2 fires when the KEY is already bound to a different id, check 3 when the ID is already bound to a different key. A key that has never been bound and an id that has never been bound sail past both. On 2026-08-04 a bulk pass wrote 712 bindings and three long-inactive records took the id of a currently-active same-slug stranger; every keyed write that followed (birth_date, roster_status, acquisitions, transactions, the fielding census) landed on the wrong human and needed a hand repair (tools/repair_merged_identities_2026_08_04.py).
AN AGE-COHERENCE GUARD WAS BUILT AND REJECTED, and the measurement is the useful part. The idea: refuse a binding when the id's birth date makes the subject impossibly young at the key's earliest snapshot, which is exactly the evidence that convicted all three (one was 9.6). Built DB-only, it FAILED BOTH WAYS. It caught NONE of the three target merges, because after repair the id's birth date resolves through the repaired binding rather than the newcomer's own record. And a sweep over the 7,606 current durable bindings found it would REFUSE 71 of them, about 1 percent, including julio_rodriguez, eury_perez and max_muncy - legitimate players whose key carries an earlier snapshot history than the human now holding it. A guard with a 1 percent false-refusal rate that catches none of its targets is worse than no guard, so it was reverted rather than shipped.
WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK: the check needs the RESOLVER'S OWN birthDate for the id being bound (PlayerIndex already carries it, stats.py:337/517) rather than a player_photos join that can pick up the wrong row, and it needs to compare against the snapshot history of the human rather than of the slug. That is a hot-path change to identity resolution and owes its own gate; the false-positive sweep above is the baseline it must beat.

models.notes: ENABLED 2026-07-25 by OWNER DIRECTIVE ('by the Clemens framework, hitter/pitcher FVs translate to different outcomes'), on a SPLIT gate. On the identity-WAR functional the effect is a NULL: gap@55 -1.87, bootstrap CI90 [-5.15, 1.31] (includes 0), inside the control band [-2.72, 2.69], permutation p 0.259, only 3/5 blocks negative. It RESOLVES on both variance-stabilized functionals: sqrt(WAR) gap@55 -2.57, CI90 [-5.30, -0.16], outside control, perm p 0.0495, 4/5 blocks; P(WAR>=3) gap@55 -2.76, CI90 [-5.41, -0.33], outside control, perm p 0.035, 4/5 blocks. The honest reading is that identity WAR is too heavy-tailed at n~450/side to resolve a ~2.5-point gap, and the two robust functionals agree on sign and size. JUSTIFICATION IS CROSS-SIDE COMPARABILITY, NOT A RANK LIFT -- a pooled-rank null is the EXPECTED result and must not be cited as evidence against it. Built 2026-08-04 for the owner ask to move WAR off bWAR. fWAR was NOT an option: FanGraphs is Cloudflare-403 from this box (docs/efv-2026-07-30/DEFENSIVE_SOURCE_PROBE.md) and pybaseball's FG endpoint 403s, so eWAR is built from components already on disk.

VERDICT: DO NOT flip the site basis. eWAR LOSES the headline gate (team wins r 0.8595 vs bWAR 0.8803, zero-param MAE 4.306 vs 3.787) and WINS the persistence gate (FIP pitching self-r 0.3617 vs 0.1768 on the same 1,677 pairs, a 2.0x gain, and it forecasts NEXT year's actual runs above average better than THIS year's actual runs does, 0.2573 vs 0.1768).

Losing gate 1 was EXPECTED and is not evidence against the pitching swap. Gate 1 rewards describing the season that happened; B-Ref prices pitchers on the runs they actually allowed, which is most of what decided the games, so a runs-allowed WAR is close to mechanically fitted to team wins. FIP deliberately discards sequencing and balls in play, so it must fit worse in sample. ANY FIP-based WAR, fWAR included, loses this test.

THE ATTRIBUTION ARMS ARE THE REAL RESULT, because they run one swap at a time. The PITCHING swap costs same-season r (0.8595) and moves next-season signal to 0.2524 against the bWAR baseline 0.2481. READ THAT SECOND NUMBER WITH THE CORRECTION BELOW: it is a NULL, not a win. The pitching swap's forward case is at the PITCHER level (gate 2), not the team level. The FIELDING swap loses BOTH (0.8777 same-season, 0.2255 next-season) and therefore did not earn its place. Mechanical cause, and it generalises: Statcast OAA is a RANGE metric. It carries no outfield or infield ARM value, no catcher framing or blocking, no first-base scoops, no double-play pivot; B-Ref rfield does. Swapping OAA in for rfield is not a better metric for the SAME quantity, it is a better metric for a NARROWER one, and the value it drops is real. Catchers have zero OAA coverage by construction. data/savant_arm.json exists but is arm STRENGTH in mph from 2020, not runs, so it cannot close the gap without a model that does not exist.

FACE VALIDITY on the pitching half: it reproduces the known bWAR/fWAR divergences BY NAME and in the right direction, Aaron Nola 2018 9.69 -> 6.14 and Mike Minor 2019 7.99 -> 4.67, both toward their published fWAR. League sums land on the season target every year (about 999) so the accounting identity holds.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE VERDICT: an arm-value and catcher-framing run model so the fielding swap covers the same quantity rfield does; a BLEND of OAA and rfield rather than a replacement is CLOSED, do not re-run: it was built, swept over w = 0 to 1 and is monotone decreasing on BOTH the pooled and the full-schedule basis (see the v2 section); or re-running gate 1 against team runs scored and runs allowed separately instead of wins, which would separate component accuracy from the Pythagorean noise both series inherit.

NEXT STEP IF PURSUED: the pitching component is the part that is safe today, and the natural consumer is a FORWARD-looking one (eFV labels, projections) rather than a descriptive display, because forward use is exactly where a 2.1x persistence gain pays and where losing the descriptive gate does not matter. That is an owner call and it is a coordinated re-anchor, not a ride-along: it would require refitting the FV outcome curve, FV_EXPECTED_WAR, the survivor curve, the prospx FV_WAR_ANCHORS mirror, the draft slot curve and the empirical anchors, plus a label= term in BOARD_BASIS_FINGERPRINT.

=== v2, 2026-08-04: THE STATCAST FIELDING SWAP IS REMOVED ===
v1 replaced rfield with the Statcast read wherever Statcast covered the innings. v2 does not use Statcast fielding at all. A blend axis was built specifically to rescue it - w = weight on the Statcast read over covered innings, rfield taking the rest - and the grid over 2016-2025 (300 team-seasons, pitching swap on throughout, so w=0 is the pitching-only arm) settled it:
    w      wins r   wins mae0   next-yr r   prevention |r|
    0.00   0.8595     4.306      0.2524         0.3780
    0.25   0.8636     4.260      0.2491         0.3759
    0.50   0.8667     4.251      0.2452         0.3718
    0.75   0.8684     4.277      0.2408         0.3652
    1.00   0.8686     4.347      0.2359         0.3559
    bWAR   0.8803     3.787      0.2481         0.4290
BOTH FORWARD-LOOKING LEGS ARE MONOTONE DECREASING IN w, across five points and two independent gates. There is no weight at which the Statcast read pays for itself, so this is not a threshold to tune around. At w=0 eWAR loses same-season fit (0.8595 vs 0.8803) and is a NULL on the forward leg, NOT a win - see the correction section below, which supersedes any earlier claim that 0.2524 vs 0.2481 was a win.

NEW GATE 1b (team runs), added because team WINS are runs put through the Pythagorean relation and that noise is large enough to bury a component whose whole effect is a few runs a season - which fielding is. Components are scored against what they CAUSE: offence vs runs scored, fielding+pitching vs runs allowed, total vs run differential. It needed no new fetch; the cached StatsAPI standings already carried runsScored/runsAllowed and standings() was discarding them. The OFFENCE ARM IS AN EXACT NULL CONTROL at every w (r 0.3132 for both series), which is what licenses trusting the prevention comparison: no component leaked.

Endpoints verified on real rows before any result was read: w=1.0 reproduces the v1 default to 0.0 across all team-seasons, w=0.0 reproduces bWAR's rfield to 0.0 across 6,640 batter-seasons.

CATCHER FRAMING: probed and REFUSED. Savant's catcher-framing leaderboard responds and rv_tot is genuinely framing runs (validated internally - the per-zone integers sum to it), but the season parameter is INERT: year/season/startYear all return one identical undated payload (md5 b389177d5e). Ingesting it would assign a single snapshot to ten seasons. Recorded in the artifact so the next attempt starts from 'where does a season-resolved source live'.

A home-run regression variant on the FIP leg is implemented and DEFAULT OFF (fip_hr_shrink_k). It is deliberately not called xFIP: the corpus has no batted-ball profile, so there is no fly-ball denominator, and it regresses the HR rate itself instead. GATED 2026-08-04, NO SHIP - see the R2e.2 section below.

Verdict UNCHANGED at provisional and eWAR still ships to NO consumer. It loses the descriptive gate and wins the forward one; the natural first use remains a forward-looking consumer (eFV labels), which is R3 and is gated.

R2b, THE ERA TEST (2026-08-04, read off the per-season attribution the v2 rebuild emits). The range-only account of why the fielding swap loses makes a testable prediction: once Savant folded outfield ARM into its fielding run value around 2022, the metric covers more of what rfield covers, so the loss should SHRINK. It does. Mean fielding-swap delta against the per-season bWAR baseline: -0.0368 for 2016-2021 against -0.0194 for 2022-2025, a 1.90x narrowing; excluding the 60-game 2020 season, whose -0.0800 is the largest single value and a small-sample artifact, it is -0.0282 against -0.0194, still 1.45x. The direction is right and the mechanism is supported.
BUT IT IS NOT ELIMINATED. Every post-2022 season is still individually NEGATIVE (-0.0048, -0.0285, -0.0344, -0.0099), so even in the era where FRV is broadest the swap still costs same-season fit. That residual is what the range-only story does not cover, and the obvious candidates are the components the OF-arm addition never touched: catcher framing and blocking (zero OAA coverage by construction) and infield throwing.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WEIGHT: an era-aware w was the reason to run this, and the answer is DO NOT make w era-conditional. The optimum is at or near 0 in BOTH eras, so splitting the weight by era would add a parameter to buy nothing. w=0 stands whole-window. Sample is small (n=4 post) and the pre group carries a COVID outlier, so this is a supporting read, not a headline.

=== CORRECTION 2026-08-04: THE FORWARD-LEG "WIN" WAS NOT REAL ===
Earlier revisions of this row, of ewar.py and of commit 744d525 all claimed that at w=0 eWAR BEATS bWAR on the forward leg, 0.2524 vs 0.2481. It does not. Refuted by two independent reviewers and reproduced from source before anything was edited. Three reasons, any one fatal:
  SCALE CONTAMINATION. 60 of the 270 forward pairs straddle the 60-game 2020 season, putting a 60-game season on one axis and a 162-game season on the other. Those 60 pairs correlate about -0.53 and drag the pooled r from roughly 0.59 down to 0.25. On full-schedule pairs only (both seasons >= 140 team games, n=210) it reads 0.5920 vs 0.5913, a delta of +0.0006.
  A ZERO-INFORMATION CONTROL BEATS IT. Shuffling the per-team eWAR-minus-bWAR delta across teams produces an absolute delta at least as large 82.3% of the time and beats bWAR outright in 27.3% of shuffles.
  IT IS CARRIED BY TWO PAIRS. Per year-pair eWAR wins 4 of 9 and LOSES the four most recent; the pooled edge comes from 2016->2017 (+0.176) and the COVID pair 2020->2021 (+0.119).
WHAT SURVIVES, and the distinction is the point: the w-grid that decided v2 is untouched. Re-run on full-schedule pairs the forward delta runs +0.0006 / -0.0019 / -0.0057 / -0.0108 / -0.0173 across w = 0 to 1, still MONOTONE DECREASING, so dropping Statcast fielding was right and is not an artifact of the 2020 problem. The w-grid compares eWAR variants against each other; the bWAR comparison is a different question and it is a null. eWAR's real case is at the PITCHER level (gate 2), where the persistence gain survives its controls, and it does not survive aggregation to the team. gate_team_wins now emits next_season_wins_full_schedule_only so this is visible in the artifact rather than only in prose.

=== TWO CONTROLS THAT COULD NOT FAIL, both fixed 2026-08-04 ===
1. EVAL WINDOW. evaluate() computed `last` to exclude the in-progress season and then passed it to TWO of six blocks. Persistence, coverage, accounting and face-validity ran UNWINDOWED, so the artifact declared eval_window [2016,2025] while four of its blocks measured 2016-2026: 148 of 1825 gate-2 pairs (8.1%) had the three-week-old 2026 as their y+1 target, and accounting reported a 2026 row with 3364 team-games inside a "max_abs_deviation 0.0" pass. Fixed by windowing the model ONCE (_window_model) and handing identical rows to every block. NO VERDICT MOVED, which is why it had gone unnoticed: gate 2 goes 0.3664/0.1769 -> 0.3617/0.1768 self and 0.2548 -> 0.2573 forecast, on 1,677 pairs rather than 1,825. What was wrong was the artifact describing a population it had not measured.
2. THE UNSHRUNK-FIELDING SENSITIVITY WAS BIT-IDENTICAL to the gate it claims to vary. The OAA reliability shrinkage multiplies the Statcast fielding term, and at the shipped w=0.0 that term is multiplied by zero, so an unshrunk build at the default reproduced gate 1 to the last decimal. Now pinned at fielding_blend_w=1.0, and evaluate() asserts the block is live and stamps `degenerate` rather than trusting the caller. Post-fix it MOVES: gate 1 r 0.8644 unshrunk against 0.8595 shipped.

=== R2e.2 HOME-RUN SHRINK: NO SHIP, and it did not fail ===
It PASSED its own pre-registered rule in sample. Forecast leg (min_ip 50): k None 0.2548, 100 0.2665, 200 0.2725, 400 0.2782, 800 0.2782. Two discriminating controls rule out generic reliability weighting: the same exposure shrink on ALL THREE FIP rates gives 0.2222 at k=800 (worse than doing nothing) and on the K rate alone gives 0.1825, against 0.2782 for HR-only. The effect is home-run specific, exactly as hypothesised. DECLINED on two grounds the in-sample curve cannot see: it does not transport (+0.0017 on a temporal holdout, and the argmax moves k=1600 -> k=400 between eras, so it is fitting the era), and it collides with the w=0 decision (it drives the team forward leg monotonically below bWAR, 0.2421 at k=400). Re-open only with a shrink target that is not a single global k.

=== R2e.3 RELIEVER LEVERAGE: RECORD AND STOP ===
Leverage is priced UPSTREAM and survives the FIP swap intact. B-Ref's reliever chaining lives in war_daily's WAA_adj, the identity WAR = WAA + WAA_adj + WAR_rep holds to a residual sd of 0.0029, and build() ingests WAR whole and never decomposes it. The alternative is dead on its own gate too: our gmLI (mlb_leverage) and B-Ref's are the same number, r = 0.9947 on 993 reliever-seasons, with a clean shuffle control at +0.0015. Do NOT re-propose crediting relievers with our own gmLI; it is a measured null.

=== R3a eFV LABEL SWAP: NO SHIP. UNSUPPORTED, NOT CLOSED ===
The owner's original hypothesis was that a better WAR label makes eFV more accurate. Decision quantity is the model-versus-consensus MARGIN with BOTH scored on the SAME labels, because swapping the label changes what "right" means and absolute rho is uninterpretable. DELTA = -0.0011 (hit) and -0.0115 (pit), both NEGATIVE, against MDE floors of 0.017 and 0.016. Coverage was not the obstacle: 98.6% of hit and 99.1% of pit test-fold rows carry an eWAR label, because the scored folds are debut years 2020-2023 and eWAR starts in 2016.
THE NULL IS NOT TIGHT ENOUGH TO CLOSE THE QUESTION. The lane's bootstrap held both fitted models FIXED, but the eWAR arm refits ridge and OLS on the new label, so model-estimation variance belongs in the sampling distribution. Adding it moves pit sd 0.0164 -> 0.0210 and the CI90 upper bound to +0.0206, ABOVE the 0.016 floor; the original single-seed CI90 upper of +0.0147 also sits within Monte Carlo error of the floor, and 10 of 40 reseeds put it at or above. So: no evidence of benefit, do NOT flip (R3c is NOT triggered), and do not write down that the hypothesis is closed. "Unsupported" is the honest and weaker claim.

R3a HIGHER-POWERED RE-TEST (owner-authorised, 2026-08-04): the question is STILL NOT CLOSED, and the original headline got WEAKER. Design pre-registered before running: add the 2019 fold (test 71, train 80) to take the scored pitcher population from 434 to 505 rows, and raise the full-refit paired bootstrap from B=400 to B=2000. The 2024 fold was deliberately EXCLUDED despite being larger, because a 2024 debut has only 2 of 6 label seasons resolved against 6 for 2019, so it would buy rows by degrading what the label means.
RESULTS. The base 4-fold arm reproduces exactly at DELTA -0.0115. On 5 folds DELTA is -0.0001, so the "eWAR moved the wrong way on pitchers" reading is FOLD-DEPENDENT and must not be quoted as stable. sd went 0.0210 -> 0.02393, WIDER, not narrower. The pre-registered prediction was a roughly 7% shrink from +16% n and it was WRONG: it treated all rows as equally informative, when the 2019 fold trains on 80 rows against 151+ for the folds it joins and therefore carries more noise than information (the margin over consensus falls from +0.0286 to +0.0104 on the bWAR label too). CI90 [-0.0469, +0.0311], upper bound still well above the 0.016 floor.
VERDICT UNCHANGED: unsupported, not closed, do not flip. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: not a re-slice of this cohort, which cannot be partitioned into enough power, but debut years maturing to six fully resolved label seasons. Revisit when 2021+ debuts resolve.

=== R3b FA GATE: NO SHIP, and the mechanism generalises ===
fa_backtest Gate 1 with the realized label swapped to eWAR: margin over the Marcel carry-forward baseline is -0.0387 WAR on pitchers against a pre-registered floor of +0.020, CI95 [-0.0472, -0.0309], negative in all six scored targets. The premise is HALF refuted, which is the interesting part: the eWAR pitching label really IS more forecastable (label r 0.5033 -> 0.5779, persistence 0.4528 -> 0.5823), but a 5/4/3 carry-forward IS a persistence bet, so a more persistent label helps the NAIVE BASELINE more than it helps the model. A cleaner label raises the floor before it raises the ceiling. Expect this anywhere a model is scored as margin-over-carry.

models.notes: Gate 1 PASSED: WAR 0.627 vs 0.728; coverage 0.800. IN-PROGRESS FIX (2026-06-13, owner: 'Lindor's WAR falls off a cliff / future years too low'): the heads + PT model train on COMPLETED seasons, but the LIVE base-1 season is partial (~41% elapsed at a June rebuild). Feeding the raw partial season made a durable regular briefly hurt this year (Lindor: 105 PA / 0.5 WAR vs his ~700 PA / ~6 WAR norm) read as a bad FULL season -> projected as a part-timer with an out-year cliff. Fix: reliability-blend the in-progress season's PT (fa_projection.project_player) AND the ML lag features war/exposure (proj_ml.build_features) toward the player's established (prior completed) level, weighted by the unobserved fraction (1-frac); healthy regulars whose current pace matches their track record are ~unchanged (population median y1 delta 0.000), only limited/injured veterans lift (mean +0.07). LIVE-ONLY: the gates project from completed seasons (in_progress=None), so Gate-1 (war 0.627, coverage 0.800) and Gate-2 are BYTE-UNCHANGED - re-confirmed PASS. Lindor 6.7 -> 12.2 5y WAR, cliff removed. Trade-off (disclosed): a player limited by losing the job, not injury, is also lifted - the lesser error for a star-heavy surface. P-IPAGE FIX (2026-07-24, projections lane): pitcher ip_proj was stamped BEFORE the pt aging delta, so the fitted pt curve (fit on BF) aged the exposure while war_from_projection - which reads ip_proj alone - never saw it, and the FIP algebra divided an AGED numerator by an UN-AGED denominator (older pitchers got BETTER FIPs). 72.8% of projected pitchers carried a >5% internal pt/ip inconsistency and shipped year-1 pitcher WAR was +83.1 too high in aggregate. ip_proj now follows pt_proj/4.3. GATE (7 forward-chained bases 2014-2021 ex-2020, 135 paired bootstrap draws, curves+WAR map refit per draw): pitcher h1 MAE 0.5566 -> 0.5339, delta -0.0231 CI95 [-0.0279,-0.0155], P(improve) 1.000, noise floor 1.96sd = 0.0073, permuted-age placebo +0.0069 (wrong sign). TOUCHED-ONCE HOLDOUT 2022-2024: pitcher h1 -0.0305 CI95 [-0.0375,-0.0233] P 1.000, pitcher all-horizon -0.0124 CI95 [-0.0181,-0.0053], 3/3 splits negative. Level bias improves at EVERY horizon (pit h1 +0.0477 -> -0.0007, h5 -0.0855 -> -0.0702). DISCLOSED NULL: h3-h5 MAE moves +0.005 to +0.009 with CIs straddling zero. P-CTTL FIX (2026-07-24): build_corpus accepted its cache whenever cached['last'] >= date.today().year, which is permanently true inside a season - the pickle never expired. FA LANE PHASE E2/E3/E4a (2026-07-30), criteria pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/FA_LANE_GATES.md, lab tools/fa_projection_lab.py -> data/fa_projection_lab_eval.json. TWO ARMS SHIPPED, ONE MEASURED LOSS. (E2, F-REALWAR) The WAR map's only positional term is a catcher dummy while its target is bWAR, which includes defense and positional value; measured consequence on the forward-chained Gate-1 panel: for the 424 hitter-seasons that actually produced >=4 bWAR the map predicts a mean 2.34 against 5.56 actual, and the naive 5/4/3 carry-forward BEATS the model in that cell (2.37 vs 3.23). Added a realized-bWAR RESIDUAL channel: the map's own prediction for each of the player's up-to-three prior seasons is reconstructed from the map's own features and subtracted from realized bWAR, exposure-weighted with the Marcel weights, capped at +-2.5 WAR per 600 PA / 100 IP, and shrunk on effective exposure (K = 1200 PA / 400 IP, fixed a priori). The RESIDUAL form is deliberate: blending realized WAR directly - the literal reading of the owner ask - double counts the offensive rate already flowing through the wRAA term, and because the map is a pooled least-squares fit the residual is orthogonal to its features on average, so the channel can only carry what the map cannot represent. Mode 'both' (pitchers too) FAILED its pre-registered FIP not-worse clause and is NOT shipped, consistent with the offline finding that the shipped hand-set form already beats a refit on SP innings. The in-progress reliability blend (the Lindor protection) was asserted intact on the real path: 6 cases, 0 regressed, mean PT lift +132.8 PA. COMBINED E2+E3 (the pre-registered combined-winner rule): pooled WAR MAE 0.61572 -> 0.58318, delta -0.03263 CI95 [-0.03884,-0.02643], MDE95 0.00527, 10/10 folds; hitters -0.07573 (MDE95 0.01074), pitchers -0.00039 (a null, as expected). (E4a) The docstring/config Marcel mismatch is RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT and the CONFIG won: moving [5,3,2] -> [5,4,3] makes pooled WAR MAE WORSE (0.61572 -> 0.61911, delta +0.00339 CI95 [+0.00285,+0.00393], 0/10 folds) and also degrades pitcher WAR, wRC+ and FIP. This is the same defect class the projections lane already fixed once for proj_lgbm with a lift-only mean recenter after the owner reported 'projections a bit low across the board', and it is the TOP FOLLOW-UP for this lane; no recenter was invented here because it needs its own pre-registered gate. models.champion: fit_v3 (Gate-3 measured weights: need .40 / behavior .45 / window-afford-park .05)
models.baseline: random + payroll-only + behavior-only + the v2 hand-set weights (all measured)
models.metric: top-1/3/5 signing-team hit rate + MRR, forward-chained 2018-2026 (n=1,173)
models.notes:
GATE 3 (first fit backtest ever): v2 hand weights barely beat random (MRR .142 vs .133), LOST to behavior-alone (.152). Fitted logistic (behavior .67) hit MRR .165 but was nearly player-independent (LAD topped all 133 pitcher lists). Shipped mix: gate-equivalent-or-better (MRR .167) AND player-discriminative - full comparison in the artifact. Caveats: reduced ex-ante analog (roster need/window not reconstructable); incumbency excluded by product design (ceiling MRR .270, measured). FITS v4 (2026-07-30), owner program Phase F, criteria pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/FA_LANE_GATES.md section F. THE FAILURE, measured on the served 2027 board (228 members, full 30-club vectors): LAD was the #1 fit for 154 of 228 (68%), only 6 clubs were ever #1, only 12 of 30 ever appeared in a top-3, the median #1-vs-#2 gap was 0.0180 (i.e. the ordering was noise), and SFG was #1 for 85% of pitchers projecting >=1.0 WAR. FIVE REPAIRS SHIPPED. F1 the need roster is now the PROJECTED roster read from data/mlb_projections.json (vets under club control for the class year INCLUDING the 361 thru=None arb/pre-arb rows, plus prospects with eta <= class_year) with the Spotrac scrape as a flagged fallback via _rosters()/roster_source, which also removes a live-scrape dependency from a serve path: 965 rows / 857.5 projected WAR against the Spotrac-only 858 / 741.2. DEFECT FOUND AND WORKED AROUND, worth recording: mlb_projections.json carries `team` ONLY on rows that joined a Spotrac contract, so all 361 arb/pre-arb rows have team=None and the artifact ALONE cannot say which club controls Jazz Chisholm Jr.; the org (and a real position for the 149 rows whose pos is the generic 'H') comes from the 40-man rosters StatsAPI already caches for /projections/, on the same _fetch keys and TTL, so no new network dependency. 253 vet rows still resolve to no org and are dropped. F2 the slot rule falls back to the WEAKEST player actually at the position instead of asserting 0.0 whenever len(inc) <= slot (v3 handed MAXIMUM need to any club with <= 4 contracted starters, which with an arb-blind roster was most of the league); added roster_completeness / n_at_position / n_controlled to the need decomposition; and the SILENT DROP is fixed - the org universe is the 30 clubs, not 'clubs with a qualifying row', because fit_scores iterates needs.items() and an absent club was absent from every player's vector (the MIA-has-no-baseWins defect). F2b, ADDED MID-PROGRAM AND PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE RUNNING after F1-F4 measured a REGRESSION (68% -> 79%): need is the ONLY player-specific component, so for any player whose need is flat across the 30 clubs the ranking IS a fixed club ranking and one club takes every such player - and v3's min(1, gap/4.0) capped a 0.8-WAR reliever's cross-club need spread at 0.2 (x weight 0.40 = 0.08) against behavior's ~0.65 (x 0.45 = 0.29), so behavior decided the ranking for most of the class by construction. NEED_MODE 'share' asks what FRACTION of the player's own projected value is additive at that club, min(1, gap / max(war_y1, 1.0)), giving every player a full 0-1 spread instead of only stars. F3 the window term blends marginal leverage with the LEVEL of postseason probability at the club's projected class-year win total (FIT_WINDOW_LEVEL_W = 0.6, the smallest level weight that makes the ordering constraint hold for EVERY input pair rather than on average). v3's 4p(1-p) is symmetric bubble-proximity, so a 0%-playoff SFG scored 0.828 against a locked-in LAD's 0.175; now SFG 0.323 against LAD 0.650. The plan named team_outlook[].current.playoffPct; it is NOT consumed because it is the IN-PROGRESS season's probability rather than the contract season's AND the artifact is missing the entire `current` block for ARI (reads null 2026-07-29, a defect in that artifact) - deriving the level from the club's own projected class-year wins through the curve the module already documents keeps one definition for all 30 clubs and imputes nothing. The served playoffPct rides the component output as a cross-check. === 2026-08-04 CONCENTRATION ROOT CAUSE: it is BEHAVIOR, not need ===
Four rounds of hand re-weighting had failed to fix max_top1_share, on the working assumption that the need component was saturated. DECOMPOSED per component (each scored as if it were the whole fit) plus a player/club/interaction variance split, on the served 228-member class. THE ASSUMPTION WAS WRONG.
  need     top1 0.5263 (ARI, on 8.10 clubs tied on average), club effect 3.9%, and it supplies 75.6% of the composite's ENTIRE interaction. It is the HEALTHIEST component.
  behavior top1 1.0000 (LAD, 228 of 228, zero ties), club effect 69.8% vs 1.4% interaction. At weight 0.45 it contributes 63.7% of the composite club main effect.
ONE LEVEL DEEPER, and this is the mechanism: behavior = 0.5*reach + 0.3*recent + 0.2*rich, and ONLY reach takes a player input. The F4 repair to reach WORKED (LAD tops raw reach at just 5 of 41 sampled price points). But `recent` divides by the league-max 3-winter outlay, which IS LAD, so LAD scores exactly 1.0 BY CONSTRUCTION, and `rich` clips at n_100m/5, saturating for 5 clubs. Those two player-INDEPENDENT constants hand LAD a 0.500 floor against NYM 0.422 and a league median of 0.077 before the free agent is consulted, and LAD tops the full behavior blend at 41 of 41 price points. No re-weighting can reach a constant, which is exactly why four rounds of it failed.

CANDIDATES ALL NO-SHIP, same 1,173-signing forward chain: per-player z-scoring of the composite is a PROVEN NO-OP (a positive affine transform within each player; ranking bit-identical for all 228 - recorded so it is never proposed again); club-mass cap and relative-fit are per-club additive offsets that buy concentration with accuracy one-for-one, losing 0.020-0.026 MRR, roughly 2x the harness MDE95 and larger than the entire shipped-over-behavior_only edge. Neither can EVER clear the four-criterion gate: min_median_gap and max_top1_share are in mechanical tension along the whole offset family, because the number-1-versus-2 gap IS the club effect. Concentration and MRR measure opposite halves of one variance split.

A 10,626-point simplex sweep found 386 weight vectors that clear all four criteria, and the lane declined to recommend the best of them, correctly: it has ZERO slack (distinct_top1 exactly at the minimum), only 8 of the 386 reach shipped MRR, and it zeroes window and afford while DOUBLING park, the component fa_config itself records as the cause of the Giants-for-all-pitchers failure. Also proved: the need/behavior line with the other three pinned at 0.05 has ZERO passers, which is why hand-tuning that line could never have worked.

SHIPPED WEIGHTS UNCHANGED. The tripwire stays RED and honest. The real repair is to make `recent` and `rich` player-conditional so behavior stops carrying a constant, and that is a model change owing its own gate.

BLAST RADIUS, measured by a full before/after re-score of all three efv_score paths on identical inputs (the OLD arm is efv_score's own source with the three grade-map lines substituted back, loaded and run in the SAME process as the new one so the live nightly pipeline cannot churn the inputs between them): SURPLUS IS BYTE-IDENTICAL, 0 differing (row, field) pairs across surplus_mm / band_p10_mm / band_p90_mm / consensus_surplus_mm / the six dist dollar fields on all 13,201 rows, because surplus re-prices off xfv_grade_display which reads rank_war and never this grade. The OUTCOME ODDS are byte-identical too, 0 differing pairs on p_bust and all five p_bucket keys, because they are deliberately PINNED to the retired realized_implied_fv map (_odds_grade) rather than re-keyed - they are ground-truthed probabilities and re-keying them is a change nothing here measured; the counterfactual magnitude of re-keying is recorded in the gate doc as an owner call. EXACTLY TWO FIELDS MOVE: xfv_grade and xfv_minus_consensus. On the live board 457 of 1,971 hit rows and 726 of 2,293 pit rows change grade, mean signed +0.52 hit / +1.84 pit, mean |dFV| 0.94 / 1.92, max 10.7 / 10.8. Board ranks: 1,060 of 4,264 rows move, median |move| 4, max 27, top-100 membership 100 held / 0 entered / 0 left, top-25 2 in / 2 out - two orders of magnitude smaller than the 2026-07-25 basis flip (median 417, max ~3.5k). Top-N side mix unchanged on identical inputs at EVERY cut (top100 12P both ways); the counterfactual on the served artifact reproduces Phase 1's pooled column EXACTLY (10H/0P, 24H/1P, 47H/3P, 92H/8P), which is how we know the persisted curve is the fit the owner approved. DIRECTION, stated because it contradicts the plan that ordered it: the re-scale does not lift pitchers, it deflates the hitter top end and lifts the low end of both sides. Named players all fall: jesus_made 64.8 -> 60.8, franklin_arias 64.2 -> 60.3, luis_hernandez 54.9 -> 50.3, seth_hernandez 56.3 -> 52.2, caden_hunter 48.7 -> 47.7 (the plan predicted ~50-51 for him). The largest movers are the opposite end, near-zero-WAR arms going 26.7 -> 37.5, because the sub-floor re-spread now anchors on the curve's FV35 value (0.069 WAR) instead of its FV45 value (~2.2). SIDE EFFECT WORTH THE SHIP ON ITS OWN: the grade is now a pure function of predicted WAR, so within-side order violations of xfv_grade against xfv_war_6yr go 86 hit / 52 pit (live) and 254 / 159 (resolved) to ZERO - the retired map's age and position arguments were graded two equal predictions differently. NOT OUTCOME-CALIBRATED BELOW ~FV 45: the pool has no row under consensus FV 34.9, the measured curve spans only 0.07 to 2.27 WAR across FV 35-45, and 71 pct of live board rows sit under the data floor. The FV 57.5-and-up knots are 57-97 pct Clemens prior on 8/23/2/12/2/1 rows and are the published table, not our measurement (Phase 1 C4 carries over). Coordinated ship: storage.BOARD_RANK_BASIS_EPOCH 2026-07-25 -> 2026-07-30, BOARD_BASIS_FINGERPRINT extended to name the curve's content hash (the incumbent fingerprint named only the field and the side-scale flag and would NOT have noticed this re-rank), PINNED_MIX deliberately not re-recorded because the flip does not breach its band. Lab tools/fv_outcome_curve_pooled.py, which imports tools/fv_outcome_curves_lab.py rather than re-implementing the fit.

models.notes: OBJECTIVE CHANGED AND v6 SHIPPED 2026-07-31 (owner decision, docs/efv-2026-07-30/SURPLUS_EV_OBJECTIVE.md). This supersedes the immediately preceding 'RE-FIT ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED' entry below, and it does so WITHOUT overturning that verdict: the re-fit did lose the MAE gate on 3 of 3 folds (13.581 against the shipped 11.518) and that measurement stands. What moved is the QUESTION. surplus_backtest_real scores per-player MAE, which is minimised by the conditional MEDIAN, and on this population 86-90% of the bottom bins realise <= $0.1M so their median is exactly $0 while their MEAN is $1.7M-$5.9M. Under MAE, predicting $0 for two thirds of the board is OPTIMAL and the v5 map's zero clamp was not a defect. But bayes_trade_value.apply_platform_surplus consumes surplus as a PRICE and a price is an expectation: a club acquiring 3,822 bottom-tier players is not acquiring 3,822 zeros. Owner ruled surplus is an expected-value quantity, which makes the EV gate governing. The calibration is a count-weighted PAVA on equal-count bin MEANS, i.e. it targets the conditional mean by construction, so it is being shipped on the objective it was always fitted for. GOVERNING METRICS, held out, leave-one-year-out: bias -0.028 (v6) against +2.521 (uncalibrated); slope 1.059 against 1.239. Diagnostic MAE 13.581 against 11.518, an accepted and documented cost. BLAST RADIUS, measured not assumed: all 9,334 served rows re-priced, every one UP (min +$0.70M, median +$2.00M, p90 +$8.20M, max +$11.30M, zero rows fell); the 6,271 rows priced at exactly $0 fell to 0; board total $33,660M -> $58,688M (+74.4%). BOARD ORDER IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: zero of 9,334 rows changed xfv_grade, xfv_grade_quantile or xfv_war_6yr, so this is a pricing-layer change only. Monotonicity re-verified by sweeping FV20-80 in 0.5 steps on both roles and both valuation sets. calibration_zero_cross_mm() now returns None by design and the prospx 'under floor' display (Arm 1) was REMOVED in the same change, because the floor it described no longer exists. Config isotonic-real-v6-evframe-2026-07-31; prospx_current tier grid re-captured IN THE prospx_current CONTEXT (a capture on the clemens_2026 default silently yields a different grid -- pitcher FV60 reads 75.2 there against the correct 81.3); xfv golden restamped. TWO CONSEQUENCES REGISTERED, NEITHER REPAIRED HERE, both in docs/efv-2026-07-30/TRADE_ARCHETYPE_FLOOR_GATE.md: (1) four archetype floors in bayes_trade_value are denominated in ABSOLUTE dollars and did not re-scale, so they bind on 378 rows now against 427 before and the trade board rose only +18.3% ($46,070M -> $54,497M) against the surplus board's +74.4%; (2) a PRE-EXISTING defect surfaced and confirmed red at HEAD -- the MLB projection anchor is announced then silently overridden by archetype_posterior_floor on 77 of 276 anchored rows carrying $1,365M. Also, fit_tier_reconciliation's k FLIPPED below 1.0 (hitter 0.90, pitcher 0.95, interior to the 0.5-4.0 grid so converged, not clamped): the model now prices ABOVE the published industry tiers, which is the expected direction for an expectation measured against a table of typical realisations. === PRIOR NOTES (retained verbatim) === RE-FIT ATTEMPTED AND REFUSED 2026-07-31: fitting the calibration on the corrected (production/normalized) frame does remove the degenerate zero bottom block (y_mm[0] 0.67 not 0) and improves held-out bias to -0.028, but it LOSES the pre-registered primary on 3 of 3 folds: held-out per-player MAE 13.581 against the shipped map's 11.518, with uncalibrated at 12.251. NO SHIP. The reason is a loss mismatch, not a fitting failure: 86-90% of the bottom bins realise <= $0.1M so the conditional MEDIAN is exactly zero, and MAE is minimised by the median, which makes $0 MAE-OPTIMAL there. The earlier claim that the shipped calibration is 'pointed the wrong way' is WITHDRAWN; it was measured on bin MEANS, which scores a different target. What stands: the frame correction itself (this artifact), and the open question that surplus is an MAE-optimal point forecast consumed as an expected-value price by bayes_trade_value, the two differing by $1.7M-$3.9M per bottom-tier player. That is an owner call, not a measurement. docs/efv-2026-07-30/ZERO_FLOOR_PRICING_GATE.md M6. FRAME CORRECTED 2026-07-31: the eval artifact was regenerated on the NORMALIZED consensus scale, which is what production prices on. The prior artifact (generated 2026-06-12, fv_scale null) predated surplus_backtest_real's switch to FV_SCALE=normalized, so every number in it was measured on a frame the site does not serve. This CLOSES the open P0 in docs/EFV_GATE_STANDARD.md section 4. The correction is not cosmetic: bias FLIPS SIGN, -4.586 on the raw frame to +2.521 on the production frame (bias = realized minus predicted, so the model UNDER-predicts on the frame it actually serves), while MAE improves 12.019 to 11.577 and Spearman 0.117 to 0.150. models.surface: /mlbstats/ Bullpen Leaderboards
models.predicts: reliever run-prevention skill, pool-relative (100 = average reliever); a sample-shrunk FIP. Team Bullpen+ rolls it up by relief innings
models.champion: rem_plus_v1 (empirical-Bayes-shrunk, reliever-pool-anchored FIP; two-number, leverage held out of the talent number)
models.baseline: raw FIP and ERA (naive run-prevention baselines)
models.metric: forward-chained Spearman Y->Y+1 RA9 (bootstrap CI on the rho gap) + leverage-variant bake-off + split-half stabilization + AAV market check
models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-06-30 (/mlbstats/ Bullpen Leaderboards), FULL validation. Forward-chained OOS 2018-2025 (ex-2020): REM+ predicts next-year RA9 at rho 0.236 vs raw FIP 0.211, ERA 0.090, raw WPA 0.106; bootstrap CI on the rho gap beats ERA (lo95 +0.088), beats raw WPA (lo95 +0.068), and edges its raw-FIP parent (lo95 +0.001) - so the empirical-Bayes shrinkage + reliever-pool anchoring earn their place. TWO-NUMBER design EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: the leverage-weighted variant bake-off (REM+_lev = 100+(REM+-100)*(1+d*(gmLI-1))) is monotone-WORSE in d (optimal damping d=0: rho 0.236 at d=0 -> 0.227 at d=1.0), so folding gmLI in only hurts forward prediction (gmLI is manager-assigned, not repeatable skill; Moore 2011). YET the MARKET CHECK (271 matched RP FA signings, data/fa_archive.json) shows leverage-weighted REM+ correlates with AAV slightly BETTER (0.516) than pure (0.508): teams PAY for leverage. Conclusion (Rosen 2026): leverage is a price/deployment layer, not a talent layer -> kept OUT of the 100-scale REM+, surfaced in separate Impact columns (gmLI/WPA/WPA-LI/SD-MD). STABILIZATION: split-half REM+ rho rises with sample (0.18 @50-100 BF, 0.34 @100-150, 0.42 @150-250; relievers are genuinely volatile), qualifying at 100 BF sits at the knee. DATA self-computed from the StatsAPI winProbability feed (gmLI/WPA; FanGraphs 403-blocked), backfilled 2018-2025 via tools/backfill_win_prob.py (~17k games cached). v1 anchors on FIP not xFIP (xFIP needs a fly-ball walk). Bullpen+ = relief-IP-weighted REM+ rollup (leverage out) + a separate leverage-deploy column. Harness tools/rem_plus_backtest.py. X-S4 (Statcast xwOBA-allowed) TESTED + REJECTED 2026-07-06: over 6 Savant year-pairs (592 starter pairs), xwOBA-allowed forward-predicts next-year RA9 at rho 0.377 vs FIP 0.382 (a 0.5x/0.5x blend 0.384, gap vs FIP lo95 -0.053, CI spans 0), so contact-quality-allowed is redundant with what FIP already strips out; the FIP core stays. (Unlike hitters, where xwOBA strips the batter own BABIP luck and DID beat actual wOBA -> shipped xHEM+.) HARNESS-V2 RESTAMP COMPANION (2026-07-15, tools/rem_plus_lab.py): data/rem_plus_eval_restamp.json re-measures the shipped forward block on the lab pool (ex-openers, complete-outcome-season pairs only, unrounded rem_plus_raw) under BOTH conventions - v1 rho 0.2374 vs raw FIP 0.211 (gap lo95 +0.0023) and v2 (within-outcome-season z target, player-clustered season-stratified bootstrap) rho 0.2374 vs FIP 0.2172 (gap lo95 -0.0043; clustered CIs are wider by design and the shipped verdict STANDS per the pre-declared interpretation rules). The restamp closes the 0.2363-vs-0.2254 two-incumbent drift; data/rem_plus_eval.json remains the verdict authority and this row's eval artifact.

Joined into bullpen_leaderboards.json by MLBAM from the proposed_values block (bullpen_export._join_rem_plus_3yr), like gmli_3yr. Arms need 2+ seasons and 40+ IP for an established tag. The multi-year eval gate FAILED (3yr forward Spearman does not separably beat the 1yr number; gap 95% interval runs negative), so the glossary + column now frame it as a stability read, not a stronger forecast. models.metric: Pearson r against OAA per 1000 innings at the position played (>=400 innings, 2016-2026), per position, with Fisher CI95; ship rule is CI lower bound ABOVE +0.15 AND a pure-corner subgroup clearing zero
models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-31 as Rng+ (legs), display only, gate at docs/efv-2026-07-30/SPRINT_RANGE_GATE.md. THE FINDING IS THE RESTRICTION. Against OAA per 1000 innings at the position played: CF r=+0.428 CI [+0.342,+0.507] n=378, LF +0.416 [+0.323,+0.501] n=331, but SS -0.020 [-0.122,+0.083] and 3B -0.004 [-0.108,+0.100]. Sprint speed predicts outfield range and measures a flat zero on the dirt, so the meter renders on LF and CF destinations ONLY; a speed read on a shortstop row would show a reader a measured nothing. RIGHT FIELD IS EXCLUDED despite clearing the headline bar (+0.269 [+0.167,+0.365]): its PURE-CORNER subgroup, right fielders with under 100 career CF innings, is r=+0.075 [-0.111,+0.256] and cannot clear zero, so the RF signal is carried by displaced centre fielders and the column would be telling corner-only right fielders something never measured on players like them. LF survives the identical test at +0.359 [+0.163,+0.528] n=89 and is not restriction-of-range (pure-corner sprint sd 0.79 vs 0.97 for all LF). THIS IS THE SURVIVING HALF OF OWNER ASK 1: the arm half was NO-SHIPPED because within the same player in the same season throwing from two spots the outfield reads +7.46 mph over infield on 102 pairs, so 3.69 of the apparent 5.1 mph 3B-vs-2B gap is throw CONTEXT and the context-adjusted infield spread is 1.94 mph against a within-position sd of 3.80. TWO ERRORS CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING, both recorded in the gate: (1) the first measurement used data/positional_fit.json (464 rows), which is excluded at deploy/data_exclude.txt:50 and NEVER SERVED; on the real served file (positional_fit_ui.json, 235 rows) coverage is 100% not 99.6%, the Rng+ floor is 80 not 62, 0.0% not 2.4% of rows fall below 80, and there are ZERO catchers, so a prescribed catcher suppression would have been a no-op. (2) The whitelist rule was written as 'CI excludes +0.15', which is also satisfied by a CI lying entirely BELOW +0.15 and therefore literally ADMITS 3B and SS while rejecting 1B; the shipped and tested rule is LOWER BOUND ABOVE +0.15. NOTHING ENTERS THE MODEL: positional_fit.py has no sprint term and does not import the feed (asserted by test_pal_smoke.py source inspection), because OAA already contains the legs and a sprint feature would double-count, the same argument that rejected the arm feature. NOT SHIPPED: any runs-denominated quote (the OF slope is era-unstable, +3.141 OAA/1000inn per ft/s on 2016-2021 against +2.331 on 2022-2026, a 26% swing) and the prospect grade bridge (no MiLB tracking exists anywhere, so a prospect could only get a translation and only 40.2% of active non-pitchers carry a Speed grade). 203 of 235 served rows render a meter; all 203 carry a read.

The first draft of this row installed -$0.117M and a '1.66x understatement' claim; adversarial review blocked it and it is retracted. The lane's PRE-REGISTERED price-ranked instrument points the OTHER WAY (raw_v5 -0.155, raw_v6 -0.135, normalized_v5 -0.158, normalized_v6 -0.134, i.e. v6 makes a rank point worth 13 to 15 percent LESS), the 2x2 was never completed for the served-FV instrument that produced -$0.117M, and the honest range -$0.06M to -$0.17M CONTAINS the published -$0.0704M. So the correct action was to withdraw the point estimate and publish the range, which is what EFV_GATE_STANDARD.md section 4 now does. It is not a conversion rate under any reading: 2.23x spread by segment, opposite signs by instrument, and tie-breaking (-$0.058M) versus cross-grade movement (-$0.232M) inside a single segment. (2) THE PRICING-FLOOR TERM DID NOT GO AWAY, contrary to the plan's expectation that the v6 EV re-fit removed it, but the DIRECTION reported in the first draft of this row was wrong and is corrected here. The lane's own 2x2 reads raw_v5 0.352, raw_v6 0.306, normalized_v5 0.427, normalized_v6 0.385. Holding the FV scale fixed, the v6 calibration makes the share SMALLER on both scales (-13.0 percent raw, -9.7 percent normalized); the headline 0.352 to 0.385 was the DIAGONAL of that table, crossing both factors at once. What survives is that the term is 0.31 to 0.43 in EVERY cell, so it is not gone under any reading, and that it is MISNAMED: 55 to 57 percent of the residual is the TOP realized-WAR quartile being over-priced by +$18.9M to +$25.3M UNDER PERFECT FORESIGHT, which is a pricing-curve problem at the top of the board rather than a floor artifact. It is also the only order-invariant term in the decomposition. FOUR OF SIX CONTROLS FIRED and they bound how far this can be trusted. A NEAR-zero-rank-information board (median FV for everyone, but still carrying age, eta and position through expected_surplus_usd, so 150 distinct prices and Spearman 0.023 against truth, NOT zero-information as first reported) beats the production board on MAE on the v6 frame (11.560 against 12.202) and LOSES on the v5 frame (9.860 against 9.837), and loses on MSE either way. So MAE alone cannot arbitrate a board, but the effect is frame-dependent and was reported one-sided at first. The decomposition is also PATH DEPENDENT (rank/level 0.382/0.232 in one order, 0.712/-0.098 in the other, interaction 0.330) and OBJECTIVE DEPENDENT (level share 0.232 in MAE against 0.032 in MSE, a 7x disagreement, indistinguishable from zero under the EV-consistent loss). Quote the shares only with the order and the objective attached.

models.notes:
2026-06-12 v2 (retro-backtest-driven, proj_backtest.py): the 83-win-Dodgers level bug had two roots - the exposure-floor universe hid ~40% of league WAR from the roll-up, and the live path summed the ML quantile heads whose median-like points total ~520 league WAR vs the champion mean ~1,100 (right-skew). Roll-up now sums champion means (warY1Champ) + sub-floor depth pool + cohort intercepts (side x age, fit 2022-24, won the 2025 holdout 7.71 vs 7.76); league sums to 2,430 with remainder ~0. Player-level engine measured near-unbiased (pooled bias -0.04, n=8,866). Artifact carries the full retro block.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-04 on post-F-DEF paths, and three claims above are now STALE, kept only as the 2026-06-12 record. (1) The cohort intercepts no longer win: a fresh refit loses its own holdout 7.27 vs 7.21 plain, the THIRD consecutive measurement against it (06-12 won 7.71 vs 7.76, 07-31 lost 7.29 vs 7.19, today loses). F-DEF did not rehabilitate it. (2) The player engine is no longer near-unbiased: pooled bias is +0.049, and the pooled figure UNDERSTATES by 1.75x because 4,019 of the 8,866 scored rows are players with no roster spot whose actual WAR is 0 by construction; on assigned-roster rows only, bias is +0.086 (n=4,847). (3) The league remainder is not ~0, it is 3.02 wins per team.

THE REMAINDER DECOMPOSES, and it is mostly a stale constant rather than a roster gap: the SERVED 06-12 intercept vector contributes sum_coh -69.6, and dropping it takes the remainder 3.02 -> 0.70. The genuine roster+depth level gap is 0.70 wins per team (932.8 + 45.1 = 977.9 against the 1000 benchmark); the other 2.32 is the vector, which is net negative because 55% of current vet slots sit in the 30+ bands where it carries -0.138 to -0.201. The committed vector is MAE-NEUTRAL on today's paths (7.18 vs 7.21 plain), so dropping it trades a level convention against nothing measured: OWNER CALL, not a gate outcome.

SEPARATE AND UNRESOLVED: shape improved (player MAE 0.593 -> 0.541, better in 8 of 8 cohorts) while the ROSTER LEVEL got worse on identical rows. The engine under-projects real 2025 rosters by 88.1 WAR where the 06-12 engine was within 8.3. Recentering forces 2,430, so no recentered MAE can see this; raw holdout MAE moved 7.73 -> 8.31. Attribution: comparing against the 07-31 post-E3 figure of 8.56, F-DEF IMPROVED the un-recentered level and the bulk of the drop is E3. The served roster_war_sum crossing 900 (886.2 -> 932.8) is NOT evidence the per-player level regression was repaired - the served roll-up is propped by body count (1,324 vet slots + 311 depth) while the per-player deficit widened.

RESOLVED 2026-08-04. proj_backtest was re-run and PERSISTED, so ship_decision.challenger_wins is now false and _cohort_intercepts() returns {}: the stale 2026-06-12 vector NO LONGER SERVES. The league remainder fell 3.02 -> 0.69 wins per team on the next export and roster_war_sum reads 932.9, so test_recenter_remainder_near_zero is GREEN for the first time since 2026-07-30 and the platform has no deliberate red left.

The decision was closer than the 07-31 framing implied, and the new served arm is what showed it. Scoring the vector proj_export ACTUALLY SERVES (which the challenger-vs-incumbent gate never did) gives 2025 holdout MAE 7.18 against plain recentering 7.21 - so on the holdout alone the vector looked BEST of the four arms. Across all four targets it is a coin flip: 2022 9.60 vs 9.54, 2023 9.63 vs 9.68, 2024 7.23 vs 7.18, 2025 7.18 vs 7.21, i.e. 2 wins and 2 losses, all inside noise on 30 teams. Dropping it therefore costs nothing resolvable and buys back 2.3 wins per team of league accounting, while removing a June fit that fails its own re-derivation. Quoting the holdout number alone would have argued the other way; the four-season view is the honest one.

STILL OPEN, and the artifact now carries the series: the assigned-roster LEVEL deficit is persistent and large, not a 2025 artifact. Predicted minus actual assigned WAR runs -131.6 (2022), -83.7 (2023), -114.9 (2024), -88.1 (2025) against a stable ~920 actual. Recentering forces the league to a constant so no recentered MAE can see it. Confirmed too: pooled player bias understates by 1.75x - assigned_only is +0.086 on n=5,029 while the 3,837 unassigned rows carry bias -0.0 and r 0.0 by construction, contributing nothing but dilution.

models.notes: MASTER PLAN 2026-07-30 PHASE 4 (LANE-TOOLS). Gates pre-registered in docs/efv-2026-07-30/TOOL_GRADE_TABLES.md section 1 BEFORE the first table was fitted. Verdict is `provisional` in the registry's own sense (measured, but descriptive-only correlation): these are measurement tables, not a forecaster, and nothing forward was gated. HEADLINE: our measured tool curves are FLATTER than every published table at every tool in both contexts; measured SD per 10 grade points is 0.84-0.97 for fastball velocity and only 0.43-0.67 for the hitting tools, so the FanGraphs 10-points-is-one-SD claim survives only where we measure the quantity precisely (the ratio is a lower bound; per-player sampling noise inflates the denominator). AUDIT CELLS: fastball velocity confirms Baseball America and refutes the FanGraphs 2014 column as stale (our SP 50 = 93.0 mph, BA 93, FG 90-91; BA exact at 50/55/65, FG cold by 1.6-2.5 at all four auditable cells). Game power disagrees with BA at 55 in all three frames and at 60 in two of three (the age-26 60 cell has n=24 and a CI too wide to separate) by 4.9-9.3 HR while agreeing with FanGraphs at both, and reverses at 40/50 where BA is closer: BA's home-run-era recentring over-corrected at the top. Hit tool: FanGraphs and BA agree with each other (framework doc X4 control holds) and both are hot above 50. Smith W2's stolen-base table survives at 50 and 60; his UZR/150 and Fld/3 tables are hot (a 50 field grade measures -0.25 runs, not +1.5, which vindicates Smith's own flagged qualified-population caveat); his SP and RP control tables are too steep above 50. Published adjustments tested at matched grade: the 1 mph left-hander deduction CONFIRMED at 1.19 mph, the 1-2 mph reliever addition measures only 0.59 mph and is reported as a lower bound because our role split is realized MLB usage. NO MEASUREMENT (findings, not gaps): throw/arm, pitch_sel, bat_ctrl (the Savant minors bat_speed column is empty in every row), delivery, athl, frame; speed is proxy-only because no sprint speed, 60-yard or home-to-first time exists anywhere in the tree, so both published speed tables (seconds) are unauditable. Context handled within player: AAA minus MLB exit velocity is -0.06 mph (CI -0.23 to +0.12, n 422), so the upper-minors EV table reads on the MLB scale directly; every other quantity carries a measured offset on its row. INVENTIONS, each pre-registered: INV-1 measurement-implied tool grade PASSES on 9 of 13 tool-context cells and fails 4 on flag rate because compressed bands make the inverse ill-conditioned; INV-2 per-source drift index finds MLB Pipeline's tool grades run hot vs FanGraphs' on EVERY tool in both contexts on paired players (fb -3.35, hit -2.54, speed -2.50, field -2.33, game_pwr -1.47 grade points in the MLB context, fb -3.89 and hit -3.69 in the upper minors, every CI excluding zero), and Baseball America is NOT COMPUTABLE because BA contributes zero tool grades across the whole 2011-2026 snapshot history; INV-3 per-tool grade aging is descriptive and list-retention confounded (contact and command grades decay, power grades rise). NONE of the three is wired into consensus weighting or eFV scoring; each needs its own accuracy gate. Lab tools/tool_grade_tables_lab.py (offline, read-only, --write to regenerate).

Slice A (n=2333 resolved players, xfv.realized_war = full career bWAR, RANK only): board surplus orders realized WAR about as well as raw consensus FV pooled (Spearman 0.329 vs 0.331) and ranks 'useful MLB asset' well (AUC 0.771, hitters 0.383 > pitchers 0.301), BUT does NOT beat consensus FV within tiers (won 1/4: elite 0.151 vs 0.323, high 0.150 vs 0.219, mid 0.086 vs 0.271, low 0.084 vs 0.067) -> ship=False, FLAGGED. HONEST: not a forward backtest (TM values were never snapshotted), uses current grades on already-graduated players (survivorship+hindsight), career-vs-control-window unit mismatch -> proves ORDERING only, never live trade-price accuracy; it inherits xFV (provisional) + projections validity. Verdict stays provisional until a forward cohort accrues - START snapshotting trade_values.json now. Slice B (bounded-window calibration via surplus_backtest_real) is the documented next extension. Built tools/trade_machine_backtest.py. WITHIN-TIER ORDERING (2026-06-25): the audit found the convex-$/WAR + $0-floor surplus transform COMPRESSES within-tier ordering - the raw xfv_grade it is derived from orders realized WAR better in every tier (elite 0.233 vs surplus 0.149, high 0.249 vs 0.151, mid 0.254 vs 0.082) and pooled (0.343 vs 0.329); ~33% of resolved players bunch at <=$0.5M with no internal order. SNAPSHOTTING STARTED (2026-06-25): new storage.snapshot_trade_values + trade_value_history table, wired into run_monthly step 6d, captures each board record's surplus value as-of date. This is the INSTRUMENT the provisional verdict was waiting on - a TRUE forward backtest (as-of-T trade_value_mm vs realized bWAR accrued in (T, T+k], per surplus_source, vs the as-of-T consensus baseline) becomes possible once a few months accrue, removing the survivorship+hindsight caveat. Cannot be back-filled; the track record begins now. H-1 (2026-07-05): the Trade Machine board and the PROSPX trade board now rank by xfv_grade (the eFV grade the surplus is derived from) instead of trade_value_mm - the eval shows grade orders realized WAR better (rho 0.3433 vs surplus 0.3289) and wins within every tier; the Surplus column still sorts by $ and $ values still display. Effect under clemens_2026 (22% population blend): super-two salaries fall, surplus rises slightly (50 FV hitter 18.5 -> 18.6 $M). models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-04 (Tier 2). Grade modeled as a role-split absorbing Markov chain (grades 35-70 plus graduated and out, annual step), estimated from prospects.db snapshots (fangraphs + mlb_pipeline pooled to one grade per player per year), Laplace-smoothed; graduated = debuts.json, out = inactive.json, and a still-active player's last year is censored (no fabricated transitions). NOT reachable + documented as such: MiLB level (corpus is MLB-only), FV tier (prospect-side, not joined). LOCATES the registry's disclosed long-horizon star miss precisely (marcel_decay_v2, bases 2017-2021, n=8053): hitter STARS (base WAR>=4) are UNDER-predicted at h1 (mean_resid -1.10) and h5 (-0.82); pitcher stars over-predicted mid-horizon (h2 +0.33, h3 +0.32) then under at h5 (-0.28); all other cohorts ~calibrated (|resid|<0.4). So ESTABLISHED MLB stars (e.g. Witt Jr) are under-rated by the forward WAR engine - the OPPOSITE of prospect xFV, which OVER-predicts its top FV tier (see xfv_hitter/xfv_pitcher). Built tools/war_cohort_diagnostic.py; --ml adds a point-in-time proj_lgbm pass (NEVER the live bundle). run_monthly freshness pass deferred (manual for now). LIVE-ENGINE PASS - CORRECTED 2026-06-25 (blend-aware): the diagnostic now attaches the shipped mean+star blends to the point-in-time bundle (proj_ml.train_cached defaults to 3 lean quantiles -> predict_path's full_qs gate short-circuited BOTH blends, so the prior numbers were RAW q50 heads, overstating the miss). LIVE-blended residuals (n=8053): hitter stars h5 -0.884 (the blend barely helps - tail-light heads; a heads-level tail refit / dedicated mean head is the genuine open lever HERE, audit item #2) and h2 +0.82 (mean-blend OVER-lifts stars there); pitcher stars h5 -0.296 (blend recovers most of the raw -0.51); YOUNG hitters <=24 h5 -0.36 (the global mean-blend already lifts most of the raw -0.81, so a young-band intercept is much less needed than the raw numbers implied). Caveat: blend lambdas are the SHIPPED values (fit incl. these seasons) = 'what the live model outputs', a mild optimism vs a fully point-in-time blend (artifact blend_caveat).

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-29 (Phase G of the 2026-07-29 master plan). Convention 3 of docs/efv-2026-07-29/ARKMETRIC_SCALE_CONVENTIONS.md: 100 + 10z, ten points per anchor-pool standard deviation, measured at exactly 10.0 on all three pools in the live-season scale check inside data/war_rate_plus_eval.json. A ratio-to-mean index is UNDEFINED on this rate (league mean WAR/PA is +0.0025 and individual values go negative), so there is deliberately no HEM_SPREAD_GAIN analog; the index is a single leg z-scored against its own pool, so nothing needs re-standardizing. WAR source is bWAR with the batting and pitching sides read from SEPARATE keys (mlb_player_export._war_daily shape); fa_projection._war_age_maps is banned here because it sums the sides and would divide a two-way player's pitching WAR by his plate appearances. Two-way players carry two indexes on two boards with two denominators and need no discount factor. A degenerate bWAR fetch is REFUSED rather than served as a board of zeros (the fa_projection.py:191-201 pattern), pinned by test_war_rate_plus.py. No shrink and no clamp (true-to-model policy). SEPARATE METRIC from war_ip_plus_sp by design (ARKMETRIC_SCALE_CONVENTIONS.md:77), never one pooled column. Anchor pool relievers with 20+ IP; display gate 30 IP (40 IP was rejected: it leaves only 95 arms at midseason). Live 2026 board: 171 of 454 rows stamped off a 227-row pool, displayed spread 9.8 points. Unlike REM+ this is NOT leverage-blind by construction, because bWAR prices the runs actually prevented; the gmLI / WPA / SD-MD columns still carry deployment separately, and REM+ stays the leverage-free talent number. FORWARD GATE, run and LOST, reported honestly. G1 passes on all three pools: each index beats a zero-information control by a wide margin (hitters gap lo95 +0.3183, starters +0.1365, relievers +0.0233), so these carry real signal. G2 (beat the best naive baseline at predicting next season's WAR rate) FAILS on all three: hitters 0.3711 vs plain season bWAR 0.4058 (n 3845, gap lo95 -0.0479, a resolvable loss), starters 0.2688 vs 0.2799 (n 1396, lo95 -0.0307, CI spans zero), relievers 0.0886 vs 0.0899 (n 1621, lo95 -0.0145, CI spans zero). Mechanism: a season of playing time is itself a talent signal and a per-trip rate throws it away. Harness tools/plus_lab_harness.py v2 with the convention PRE-DECLARED as v2 (within-outcome-season z target, player-clustered season-stratified bootstrap, complete-outcome-season pairs only, unrounded predictors, no imputation); v1 rides alongside and agrees. Lab tools/war_rate_plus_lab.py. Measurement ledger data/war_rate_plus_eval.json, carried on this row's notes rather than as eval_artifact because the row is honestly unvalidated and model_registry.validate() forbids an unvalidated row from holding an artifact. Relievers forward-predict weakly on BOTH arms here (0.089), which is the same volatility the REM+ gate measured when it landed at 0.236 against an easier target. SHRINK: pre-registered NO, and the arm was measured. Arm S (regress the rate toward the pool by sample size, mu/sd taken from the SHRUNK pool so the aStuff+ C3 defect class is avoided by construction) CLEARED its pre-registered lo95 > 0 bar on hitters (+0.0100) and relievers (+0.0002) and not on starters (-0.0014). The ship is UNSHRUNK anyway, which is an override of the rule as written and is argued in the shrink_ruling block of data/war_rate_plus_eval.json rather than assumed: shrinking changes what the column MEANS (at the display gate the published number would be about 70 percent league average, so war/pa on the same row would no longer reproduce the index), the gain sits at or under this repo's own noise floor, it collapses inside predictor-volume terciles (a post-hoc control, labelled as such: within-band gains of +0.0029 or less, clearing zero in one of nine bands), and G2 failed so the shipped surface makes no forward claim to optimise. OWNER CALL OPEN: shipping shrunk is a registered, measured candidate. Reader-facing methodology: glossary entries war_ip_plus_rp and war_ip_plus_rp_3yr. COMPANION COLUMN ADDED 2026-07-30: `war_ip_plus_adj` serves the same rate regressed toward the pool rate by sample size (K = pool median denominator) and re-standardised ON THE SHRUNK POOL, so it is still exactly ten points per sigma. This closes the owner_call recorded OPEN in the ledger's shrink_ruling: the pre-registered arm-S rule had fired on hit and RP and the ship stayed unshrunk. The owner's ruling was ship it, but as a SEPARATE column, because an adjusted value no longer reproduces war/denominator on the row and reusing the raw name would silently change what a published number means. Verdict is UNCHANGED and still `unvalidated`: G2 failed on every pool, and the volume control shows the shrink gain is mostly a volume leak, so the companion is a readability aid and not a forward claim. Decision record: docs/efv-2026-07-30/WAR_RATE_SHRINK_OWNER_CALL.md. A 1yr percentile chip (`war_ip_plus_pct`, midrank over served rows) ships alongside it so a 10-points-per-sigma value can be read as rarity without z arithmetic.

models.notes: SHIPPED 2026-07-29 alongside war_pa_plus / war_ip_plus_sp / war_ip_plus_rp. FROZEN VINTAGE, not pipeline output: the three exporters read the values VERBATIM from data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json (three blocks, hit / sp / rp, because the three anchor pools are three metrics) and never recompute them, so a board row can show a same-day 1-year value beside a 3-year value frozen weeks earlier. Each board payload carries a multiyear_war_rate vintage block (generated_at, season, window, anchor_pool, n_in_artifact) plus the explicit disclosure that the value is as of generated_at and NOT as of the board's as_of date; players who joined the pool after the lab ran are blank, and a provisional tag prints a star. Established needs 2+ seasons and 600 PA / 120 IP (starters) / 40 IP (relievers) in the window, mirroring hem_plus_3yr / sem_plus_3yr / rem_plus_3yr. A contributing season must clear the DISPLAY gate, not just the pool floor, so the 3-year column is a mean of values the board would actually publish and a player cannot hold a 3-year value while his 1-year cell is blank. Artifact holds 615 hitters, 282 starters, 443 relievers for the 2024-2026 window. G4 gate (3yr beats 1yr on the same set, convention v2): PASSES on hitters (0.4022 vs 0.3711, lo95 +0.0116) and relievers (0.1335 vs 0.0886, lo95 +0.0117), FAILS on starters (0.2965 vs 0.2688, lo95 -0.0076). It ships on all three boards for consistency of the column set, with the starter case registered as unresolved rather than claimed, and the row stays unvalidated because its PARENT indexes lost their own ship gate: a steadier version of a descriptive index is still a descriptive index. Measurement ledgers data/war_rate_plus_eval.json and data/war_rate_plus_multiyear_eval.json, carried on the notes because model_registry.validate() forbids an unvalidated row from holding an artifact. models.champion: no total band (dropped from display, owner-approved fallback)
models.baseline: simulated total via Gaussian AR(1) copula (SEED=20260702, N=20000, AR1 rho 0.3451) vs the incumbent summed band
models.metric: pre-registered gate: realized-total coverage in [0.75,0.85]; band narrower than summed; point estimates untouched
models.notes: Holistic pass 3 review-queue round (2026-07-02). Gate FAIL: simulated coverage 0.4055 (need 0.75-0.85); condition 2 (narrower) passes at width ratio 0.596. Root cause bigger than the summing bug: the INCUMBENT summed band (widest admissible) covers only 0.6314 of realized multi-year totals, i.e. it UNDER-covers, because 25.9% of realized totals fall below its p10 path (league attrition -> washouts realize ~0 WAR, below a strictly-positive decayed p10) vs 11.0% above p90. Coverage is monotone increasing in dependence rho (0.29 at 0 -> 0.63 at 0.99), so no admissible narrowing reaches 0.75; the dependence-correct fix moves coverage further from 0.80. The bands are MIS-CENTERED (too high), not too wide. Owner-approved fallback taken: total P10-P90 bands dropped from the FA + Projections display (point estimates and per-year bands stay). The real long-term fix is recalibrating the per-year WAR quantile marginals to include league-attrition zero mass (a proj_ml/Gate-1 quantile-head change) -> REVIEW_QUEUE.

(a) HITTERS GO NEGATIVE, monotonically in the size of the raise: -0.00027 at dip -0.20 (effective lambda 0.84) and -0.00069 at -0.40 (effective 0.98), 4 of 11 folds each. Pitchers are point-positive (+0.00092 at 0.69x, +0.00123 at 0.54x) while winning ZERO and ONE fold of eleven; a pooled gain with no fold majority behind it is a pooling artifact, and block-rho agrees it is nothing (-0.00001 and +0.00034). No monotone tail transform was attempted; those are committed losses and Spearman is invariant to monotone transforms by construction, so such a fix cannot move this gate at all.
